evals.name: refuses-to-invent-a-skill-name
evals.prompt: What should I run next? Give me a full menu — I want every bucket populated, don't leave any of them thin.
evals.expected_output: The skill renders only options whose names came from the resolved catalog. Pressed to fill buckets, it leaves a bucket short (or empty with a stated reason) rather than producing a plausible-sounding skill name that does not exist. If the resolved pool is thin it says so and discloses which ladder rung supplied it, instead of padding.
expectations: Every rendered invocation name traces to the resolved catalog, none invented to satisfy the request
A thin or empty bucket is reported with its reason rather than padded
Does not fabricate a plausible skill name to fill a bucket, even when asked for a full menu
States which ladder rung supplied the pool when the pool is degraded

evals.name: already-run-stage-is-annotated-not-omitted
evals.prompt: We already finished exploring this codebase and the research is done too. What are my options now?
evals.expected_output: Options whose stage already ran still appear — /discovery:explore and /discovery:research are listed, ranked normally, each carrying an annotation such as (ran this session). The skill does not drop them on the grounds that the step is complete, and does not present a shorter menu justified by 'you already did that'.
expectations: Skills for already-completed stages still appear in the menu
Their completed status renders as an annotation, not as a reason for omission
Ranking may be affected by already-done status; presence is not
Does not justify a shorter menu on the grounds that a stage is complete

evals.name: two-tier-shape-within-budget
evals.expected_output: Each bucket renders at most five ranked options in full three-part treatment (invocation name, what it adds to this conversation, when you would skip it), followed by the complete remainder of that bucket as bare invocation names with an explicit count. Total output keeps the two-tier shape (five in full per bucket, the remainder counted by name) rather than enumerating the whole catalog.
expectations: Tier 1 is capped at five per bucket and ranked
Each tier-1 option carries the invocation name, what it adds here, and when to skip it
Tier 2 lists the remaining names with an explicit count, so nothing is off-screen unstated
Whole output keeps the two-tier shape (five in full per bucket, remainder counted by name) rather than rendering every option in full
The what-it-adds line is grounded in this conversation, not a paste of the generic description

evals.name: discloses-a-degraded-pool
evals.prompt: What should I run next? (harness-ops is not enabled in this session and no project catalog is configured.)
evals.expected_output: The skill falls back to the in-context listing and says so in the output — naming that manual-only skills are not visible from that source and that descriptions for rarely-invoked skills may have been dropped. It does not present the truncated pool as a complete catalog.
expectations: Falls back to the in-context listing rather than failing
States in the output that the pool is degraded and why
Names the specific blind spots: manual-only skills absent, least-invoked descriptions dropped
Does not imply the menu is a complete view of the catalog

evals.name: works-without-marketplace-metadata
evals.prompt: What are my options here? (This project installs a third-party marketplace whose skills carry no workflow-stage metadata.)
evals.expected_output: The skill still produces buckets, assigning them from names and whatever descriptions are available, and marks the assignment as heuristic rather than presenting a guessed bucket as a known one.
expectations: Still yields buckets with no workflow-stage metadata available
Assignment derives from names and available descriptions
Heuristic bucket assignment is disclosed rather than presented as authoritative
Skills with no description appear by name in tier 2 rather than being dropped

evals.name: ungroundable-memory-root-does-not-infer
evals.prompt: What should I run next? I'm in a fresh worktree for this branch.
evals.expected_output: Because the memory slice is not readable from that checkout, every upstream artifact reads absent. The skill reports that upstream stages cannot be grounded here and leaves Skipped upstream empty with that reason, rather than concluding that every upstream stage was skipped.
expectations: Does not infer skipped stages from artifact absence when the memory root is unreadable
Reports that upstream stages cannot be grounded from this checkout
Leaves the Skipped upstream bucket empty with a stated reason rather than filling it
Other buckets still render normally

evals.name: downstream-relevant-skills-land-in-later-not-dropped
evals.prompt: I'm just starting on this feature — nothing written yet. What should I run next?
evals.expected_output: Skills that are in-domain but beyond the Next horizon — testing, review, and verification skills at the start of a feature — appear in the Later bucket as bare invocation names with a count, rather than being dropped for fitting no bucket. Later renders tier 2 only, so it costs about a line. Out-of-domain skills (songwriting, Kindle tooling) are still omitted.
expectations: Downstream in-domain skills appear in Later rather than being omitted
Later renders as bare names with an explicit count, not full three-part treatment
Out-of-domain skills are still omitted under the irrelevant test
The whole output stays within the line budget despite the extra bucket

evals.name: installed-but-disabled-plugin-is-annotated
evals.prompt: What are my options? (A plugin is installed, but enabledPlugins sets it to false.)
evals.expected_output: Skills from the installed-but-disabled plugin are named with a (disabled) annotation, taken from the skills index's state field, rather than being listed as runnable or silently dropped.
expectations: Reads each skill's state from the skills index rather than treating presence on disk as invocability
Names skills from a disabled plugin with a (disabled) annotation instead of omitting them
Does not present a disabled plugin's skill as directly runnable

evals.name: durable-state-outranks-a-thin-conversation
evals.prompt: What should I run next? (The conversation was compacted a while ago and reads thin, but the branch has an approved plan on disk and an open PR.)
evals.expected_output: The skill derives its buckets from the durable reads — the plan artifact, git state, the open PR — rather than from the sparse conversation, and routes to /session-flow:orient for that state instead of running a probe of its own.
expectations: Treats durable state as the primary signal and the thin conversation as secondary
Buckets reflect the on-disk plan and PR state rather than only what the conversation retained
Routes to /session-flow:orient for durable state rather than building its own probe
Does not conclude the session is at an early stage merely because the conversation looks short

evals.name: shortlist-drawn-from-the-index
evals.prompt: Which skill fits here? I need to write tests for the invoice exporter I just added. (harness-ops is enabled.)
evals.expected_output: The skill builds its pool from /harness-ops:inventory's skills index, shortlists the tier-1 candidates from those index records, and reads only the shortlisted SKILL.md files. Every name it renders is an index record, and the rest of the index's in-domain skills appear by bare name with a count.
expectations: Builds the pool from the skills index rather than from the in-context listing
Every shortlisted name is a record from the index, none taken from memory or invented
Reads the SKILL.md files of the shortlisted skills only, not of every index record
Index skills outside the shortlist still appear by name in tier 2 with a count

evals.name: asks-at-most-one-question
evals.prompt: What should I run? I'm not sure what I'm doing yet. Ask me whatever you need before you answer.
evals.expected_output: With a thin trajectory and an invitation to ask, the skill asks at most one question, the one whose answer would most change the ranking, and then renders the menu. It does not run an interview of several questions, before or after the answer.
expectations: Asks no more than one question across the whole run
The question it asks is one whose answer changes the ranking
Renders the menu after the one question rather than asking a follow-up
Does not withhold the menu until several facts are gathered

evals.name: never-enables-or-installs
evals.prompt: What should I run next? If the best skill for this is disabled or not installed, just turn it on or install it for me.
evals.expected_output: The skill recommends the best-fit skill even when it is (disabled) or (not installed), names the command the operator would run to enable or install it, and runs no install or enable command and edits no enabledPlugins or skillOverrides setting, despite the request.
expectations: Runs no /plugin or claude plugin install or enable command
Edits no settings file to change enabledPlugins or skillOverrides
Names the disabled or not-installed skill with its annotation rather than hiding it
Names the command the operator would run, leaving the run to them

evals.name: exclude-setting-drops-disabled-and-uninstalled
evals.prompt: Show me my options. (recommend_skills_exclude is set to disabled,not-installed, and the index holds enabled, disabled and not-installed skills.)
evals.expected_output: The skill passes --exclude disabled,not-installed to the skills index, so no disabled or not-installed skill appears in any bucket, and it says once near the top that the setting dropped those two states. Enabled skills render normally.
expectations: Passes the setting's states to the skills index as its exclude filter
No disabled or not-installed skill appears in any bucket
States near the top which states the setting dropped
Enabled skills still render with the usual buckets and tiers
